The '''2013–14 season''' was the [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|110th season]] in '''[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]]''''s history and their 83rd consecutive season in [[La Liga]], the top division of [[Football in Spain|Spanish football]]. It covered a period from 1 July 2013 to 30 June 2014, and ended with the club clinching a unique [[Double (association football)#European cup double|European cup double]].

The team competed for a record 33rd [[2013–14 La Liga|La Liga]] title and entered the [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] for the 17th successive season, competing for a record 10th title. They also entered the [[2013–14 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]] in the round of 32. Real Madrid's shirt sponsor for this season was [[Emirates (airline)|Emirates]], having replaced [[Bwin.Party Digital Entertainment|Bwin.com]]. The club's major signing of the summer window was the long-awaited transfer of [[Gareth Bale]] from [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] for €100&nbsp;million.<ref name="realmadrid2">{{cite news|url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/all-about/gareth-bale-transfer|title=Gareth Bale transfer|date=1 September 2013|work=Daily Mirror|location=London|access-date=1 September 2013}}</ref>

In new manager [[Carlo Ancelotti]]'s first season at the club, Real Madrid fought on all three fronts for the [[Treble (association football)|continental treble]]. Despite leading in the league standings on multiple occasions, Madrid ultimately finished in third place (level on points with [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] and three behind cross-city rivals [[Atlético Madrid]]), collecting 87 points in total and scoring a league-high 104 goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2075051-real-madrid-claims-la-decima-with-champions-league-win-over-atletico-madrid|title=Real Madrid Claims 'La Decima' with Champions League Win over Atletico Madrid|publisher=[[Bleacher Report]]|quote=The four goals for Real Madrid—who led La Liga with 104 goals this season—were the most in a Champions League final since AC Milan defeated FC Barcelona 4-0 in 1994.|date=27 May 2014}}</ref> By that time, ''Los Blancos'' had already secured the [[2014 Copa del Rey Final|Copa del Rey]] – against rivals Barcelona – in April, with Bale scoring the winner.<ref>{{cite news|last=Lowe|first=Sid|title=Real Madrid's Gareth Bale gallops past Barcelona to land Copa del Rey|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/apr/16/barcelona-real-madrid-copa-del-rey-match-report-gareth-bale|access-date=30 April 2014|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=16 April 2014}}</ref> The major breakthrough came in the UEFA Champions League, where Real returned to the [[2014 UEFA Champions League Final|final]] after 12 years, having beaten defending champions Bayern Munich 5–0 on aggregate in the semi-finals.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bayern Munich 0–4 Real Madrid|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27193338|access-date=30 April 2014|work=BBC Sport|date=29 April 2014}}</ref> In the final, they defeated then-recently-league winners Atlético Madrid 4–1 [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|a.e.t.]] to clinch their tenth European Cup (first since 2002) and become the first team to win ten European Cups/Champions League titles, an achievement known as "''La Décima''".<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid make history with La Decima|date=26 May 2014|url=http://www.euronews.com/2014/05/26/real-madrid-make-history-with-la-decima/|publisher=euronews.com|access-date=26 May 2014}}</ref> Real's attacking trio of Bale, [[Karim Benzema|Benzema]] and [[Cristiano Ronaldo|Cristiano]], dubbed the BBC, finished the season with 97 goals.<ref>{{cite news |title=200 goals for the BBC |url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/09/200-goals-by-the-bbc |publisher=Real Madrid CF |date=24 October 2015 |access-date=3 December 2021}}</ref>

This season was the first since [[2005–06 Real Madrid CF season|2005–06]] without Argentinian striker [[Gonzalo Higuaín]], who left to join [[S.S.C. Napoli|Napoli]], and the first since [[2009-10 Real Madrid CF season|2009-10]] without German midfielder [[Mesut Özil]] who departed for [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]].

==Season overview==
===Pre-season===
Real Madrid started the summer without a manager, as [[José Mourinho]] departed to manage [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]. On 25 June, [[Carlo Ancelotti]] was officially announced as Real Madrid's new manager for the next three seasons. He appeared for his first press conference in front of the media on 26 June.<ref name="Ancelotti">{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23047006 |title=Carlo Ancelotti named Real Madrid boss, Laurent Blanc joins PSG |work=BBC Sport|date=25 June 2013 |access-date=25 September 2013}}</ref>

On 3 June, Real Madrid announced its first signing of the season by exercising the buyback option for [[Dani Carvajal]] from [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] for €6.5&nbsp;million.

On 10 June, Real Madrid announced the signing of former youth system loanee [[Casemiro]] from [[São Paulo FC|São Paulo]] for €6&nbsp;million.

On 27 June, Real Madrid announced its first major signing of the season with [[Isco]] from [[Málaga CF|Málaga]] for €30&nbsp;million.

On 10 July, Real Madrid agreed a contract extension with defender [[Nacho (footballer, born 1990)|Nacho]], keeping him in the club for four more years.

On 11 July, Real Madrid announced the sale of [[José Callejón]] to [[S.S.C. Napoli|Napoli]] for €10&nbsp;million.

On 12 July, [[Asier Illarramendi]] from [[Real Sociedad]] became the fourth signing for Real Madrid for €32.2&nbsp;million, penning a six-year deal. He was the fifth player in the first team that won the [[2013 UEFA European Under-21 Championship]] last June with [[Spain national under-21 football team|Spain]].

On 21 July, Real Madrid began its pre-season campaign against English Second Division side [[A.F.C. Bournemouth|AFC Bournemouth]]. This was Carlo Ancelotti's first game in charge, with Madrid winning 6–0. [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] scored a brace and [[Sami Khedira]], [[Gonzalo Higuaín]], [[Casemiro]] and [[Ángel Di María]] chipped in the other goals. Real Madrid also announced the sale of [[Raúl Albiol]] to Napoli for €11&nbsp;million.

On 24 July, Real Madrid played its second pre-season match against [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]], coming from two goals down to draw 2–2 with goals from Casemiro and [[Álvaro Morata]]. Madrid also agreed on a contract extension with [[Jesé]] which would keep him with at the club for four additional years.

On 25 July, Real Madrid agreed a contract extension with [[Denis Cheryshev]], keeping him with the club for four more years.

On 27 July, Real Madrid faced [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]], Ancelotti's former club, winning 1–0, with [[Karim Benzema]] scoring the lone goal. Also, Real Madrid announced the sale of [[Gonzalo Higuaín]] to Napoli for €40&nbsp;million.

On 1 August, Real Madrid played its first match in the [[International Champions Cup]] (ICC) against the [[LA Galaxy]], recording a 3–1 victory with a goal from Ángel Di María and two from [[Karim Benzema]].

On 3 August, Real Madrid faced [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] in the ICC semi-finals, beating them 2–1, with [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] and [[Mesut Özil]] scoring the goals.

On 7 August, Real Madrid faced Chelsea in the ICC final, led by former manager José Mourinho. Madrid recorded a 3–1 victory, with a brace by Cristiano Ronaldo and a goal from [[Marcelo (footballer, born 1988)|Marcelo]] capping a balanced team effort for ''Los Blancos''.

On 10 August, Real Madrid played its final pre-season match against Italian squad Inter. ''Los Merengues'' got goals from [[Kaká]] and Ronaldo and also a [[Ricky Álvarez]] own goal in a 3–0 victory.

On 1 September, Madrid reached an agreement for the transfer of [[Gareth Bale]] from [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] for a [[List of most expensive association football transfers|world record transfer fee]] of £85.3&nbsp;million (€100&nbsp;million).<ref>{{cite web |title=Real Madrid Sign Midfielder Gareth Bale For World-Record $132 Million |url=http://newyork.cbslocal.com/2013/09/02/real-madrid-sign-midfielder-gareth-bale-for-world-record-132-million/ |website=CBS News New York |date=2 September 2013 |access-date=2 September 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23538218 |title=Gareth Bale joins Real Madrid from Spurs in £85m world record deal |website=BBC Sport |date=1 September 2013}}</ref>

Concluding the summer transfer window, Real Madrid had signed five players, as well as promoting three more from the youth system. Madrid had spent €165.5&nbsp;million in the window and generated €108.5&nbsp;million from sales, resulting in a net loss of €57&nbsp;million.<ref>[http://www.managingmadrid.com/2013/9/3/4688976/real-madrid-summer-2013-transfer-window-recap Real Madrid Summer 2013 Transfer Window Recap – Managing Madrid<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

===August===
Real Madrid officially kicked off its [[2013–14 La Liga|La Liga]] campaign on 18 August, playing home to [[Real Betis]]. Ancelotti fielded a 4–3–3 formation, while playing a style of attacking football, like that of José Mourinho's tactics. Real Madrid went on to win the match 2–1, with goals from Karim Benzema and debutante Isco, ensuring Ancelotti got off to a winning start.

Madrid's second match of the season – and final match of August – was a 0–1 away win at [[Granada CF|Granada]], where a goal from Benzema ensured the victory for the club.<ref>[http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1330157833511/noticia/Cronica/0-1:_A_Benzema_goal_earns_victory.htm Real Madrid CF | Official Website] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130827060812/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1330157833511/noticia/Cronica/0-1%3A_A_Benzema_goal_earns_victory.htm |date=27 August 2013 }}</ref>

===September===
Madrid's third match of the campaign was a 3–1 home win against [[Athletic Bilbao]], with a brace from Isco and a goal from Cristiano Ronaldo sealing the deal for ''Los Blancos''.<ref>[http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1330158310037/noticia/Cronica/3-1:_Isco_and_Ronaldo_earn_Madrid_victory.htm Real Madrid CF | Official Website] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130903202254/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1330158310037/noticia/Cronica/3-1%3A_Isco_and_Ronaldo_earn_Madrid_victory.htm |date=3 September 2013 }}</ref>

Madrid was unable to progress up the table, recording a 2–2 away draw against [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]]. Although there were goals from both of Madrid's world record signings, Gareth Bale and Cristiano Ronaldo, two goals from [[Cani (Spanish footballer)|Cani]] and [[Giovani dos Santos]] held Real to a draw.<ref>[http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1378985695236/noticia/Cronica/2-2:_Bale_and_Ronaldo_score_as_Madrid_draw.htm Real Madrid CF | Official Website] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130918043229/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1378985695236/noticia/Cronica/2-2%3A_Bale_and_Ronaldo_score_as_Madrid_draw.htm |date=18 September 2013 }}</ref>

Madrid's third match of September was the club's opening [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] away clash with Turkish side [[Galatasaray S.K. (football)|Galatasaray]]. The match turned out to be a goal fest, with Madrid producing six out of the seven goals scored. A hat-trick from Cristiano Ronaldo, two from Benzema and one from Isco ensured the Madrid side a 1–6 victory.<ref>[https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/020d-0e862b809737-82dda56e4d70-1000--six-goal-madrid-overwhelm-galatasaray/ Six-goal Madrid overwhelm Galatasaray – UEFA Champions League – News – UEFA.com<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

In Real's fourth match of September, their fourth match of the Liga campaign, Madrid recorded a 4–1 home win against [[Getafe CF|Getafe]], following a brace from Ronaldo, a goal from [[Pepe (footballer, born 1983)|Pepe]] and a goal from Isco ensured the Madrid side the victory.<ref>[http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1379626001530/noticia/Cronica/4-1:_Ronaldo_leads_rout_with_brace.htm Real Madrid CF | Official Website] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130925033543/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1379626001530/noticia/Cronica/4-1%3A_Ronaldo_leads_rout_with_brace.htm |date=25 September 2013 }}</ref>

''Los Blancos'' then travelled away to [[Elche CF|Elche]], coming home with a 1–2 win with two goals from Ronaldo.<ref>[http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1380044927183/noticia/Cronica/1-2:_Two_Ronaldo_goals_beat_Elche.htm Real Madrid CF | Official Website] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130928080020/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1380044927183/noticia/Cronica/1-2%3A_Two_Ronaldo_goals_beat_Elche.htm |date=28 September 2013 }}</ref>

Madrid then faced rivals [[Atlético Madrid]] in ''[[Madrid Derby|El Derbi madrileño]]''. A [[Diego Costa]] goal in the 11th minute was all that was needed for Atlético, securing a 0–1 win against their rivals.<ref>[http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1380335484698/noticia/Cronica/0-1:_Real_Madrid_kept_trying_to_the_end.htm Real Madrid CF | Official Website] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130930212524/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1380335484698/noticia/Cronica/0-1%3A_Real_Madrid_kept_trying_to_the_end.htm |date=30 September 2013 }}</ref>

===October===
Real Madrid opened October with their second Champions League clash, this time against Danish side [[F.C. Copenhagen|Copenhagen]] at the Santiago Bernabéu. Braces from both Ronaldo and Di María produced the goals for Madrid, who won 4–0.<ref name="UEFA">[https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/025a-0ea8be855ee1-38a8e9cc8813-1000--kobenhavn-bow-to-madrid-and-two-goal-ronaldo/ København bow to Madrid and two-goal Ronaldo – UEFA Champions League – News – UEFA.com<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

Madrid travelled to [[Levante UD|Levante]], recording a 2–3 away win, with goals from [[Sergio Ramos]], Álvaro Morata and Ronaldo, coming back from 2–1 down.<ref>[http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1380842369534/noticia/Cronica/2-3:_Comeback_in_a_heart-stopping_match.htm Real Madrid CF | Official Website] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131005222458/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1380842369534/noticia/Cronica/2-3%3A_Comeback_in_a_heart-stopping_match.htm |date=5 October 2013 }}</ref> Real Madrid then hosted [[Málaga CF|Málaga]] in a 2–0 home win, with goals from Di María and Ronaldo.<ref>[http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1382045550456/noticia/Cronica/2-0:_Deserved_win_and_minds_turn_to_Juventus.htm Real Madrid CF | Official Website] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131020075508/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1382045550456/noticia/Cronica/2-0%3A_Deserved_win_and_minds_turn_to_Juventus.htm |date=20 October 2013 }}</ref>

''Los Blancos'' then began their third Champions League group clash, this time against Italian side [[Juventus FC|Juventus]]. Ronaldo opened the scoring, netting in the fourth minute, while [[Fernando Llorente]] equalized a mere ten minutes later for Juve, leveling the score at 1–1. A penalty was awarded to Madrid in the 29th minute, which was successfully converted by Ronaldo. The game ended at 2–1 to Madrid.<ref name="UEFA"/>

Real Madrid then travelled away to [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] to contest ''[[El Clásico]]''. Goals from [[Neymar]] and [[Alexis Sánchez]] gave the Catalan side the lead, but a stoppage time goal from [[Jesé]] after a brilliant solo run by Ronaldo resulted in Barça only holding a one-goal deficit against Madrid.<ref>[http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1382627405621/noticia/Cronica/2-1:_Harsh_result.htm Real Madrid CF | Official Website] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029210648/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1382627405621/noticia/Cronica/2-1%3A_Harsh_result.htm |date=29 October 2013 }}</ref>

Real Madrid then hosted [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]], a match which proved to be a ten-goal thriller. A hat-trick from Ronaldo, along with a brace from Bale and Benzema, ensured ''Los Blancos'' a deserved 7–3 win.<ref>[http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1383154713452/noticia/Cronica/7-3:_Goal-fest_at_the_Bernabeu.htm Real Madrid CF | Official Website] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131102184011/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1383154713452/noticia/Cronica/7-3%3A_Goal-fest_at_the_Bernabeu.htm |date=2 November 2013 }}</ref>

===November===
Real Madrid opened November with a tight 2–3 away win against [[Rayo Vallecano]]. Two goals from Ronaldo, along with one from Benzema, gave ''Los Blancos'' the win.<ref>[http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1383177568985/noticia/Cronica/2-3:_Win_at_Vallecas_with_a_Ronaldo_brace.htm Real Madrid CF | Official Website] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131104185851/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1383177568985/noticia/Cronica/2-3%3A_Win_at_Vallecas_with_a_Ronaldo_brace.htm |date=4 November 2013 }}</ref>

Madrid faced Juventus in another Champions League group match, this time away. The game ended 2–2, with goals from Ronaldo and Bale, while [[Arturo Vidal]] and Fernando Llorente scored for the Italian side.<ref name="ReferenceA">[https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/020f-0e87344576ea-4156919134b9-1000--juventus-fight-back-to-hold-madrid/ Juventus fight back to hold Madrid – UEFA Champions League – News – UEFA.com<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

Real then faced [[Real Sociedad]] at the Santiago Bernabéu, with Madrid almost finishing the match in the first half, putting away four goals. The goals before the break included a brace from Ronaldo, one from Benzema and one from [[Sami Khedira]]. Ronaldo completed the hat-trick in the second half, with the game ending 5–1 to Real.<ref name="ReferenceA"/>

Real faced Galatasary again in another Champions League group clash, this time at home, with Madrid winning 4–1. Sergio Ramos got dismissed near to the half-time break, but a consistent Madrid side held on with goals from Bale, Di María, Isco and [[Álvaro Arbeloa]] giving the Spanish giants the victory, along with ensuring the Madrid side a place in the knockout phase of the Champions League.<ref>[https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/020f-0ea091e215fe-d3d36b00b421-1000--ten-man-madrid-make-sure-of-knockout-place/ Ten-man Madrid make sure of knockout place – UEFA Champions League – News – UEFA.com<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

On the 27th, defensive midfielder Sami Khedira suffered a season-long injury playing in an international match for [[Germany national football team|Germany]] against [[Italy national football team|Italy]]. The injury was described as a "huge shock" from teammate [[Xabi Alonso]].<ref>[http://www.goal.com/en/news/12/spain/2013/11/22/4424601/alonso-khedira-injury-a-huge-shock Alonso: Khedira injury a huge shock – Goal.com<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

November turned out to be a month in which Madrid went undefeated in all competitions, as Real closed November with a 4–0 home win against [[Real Valladolid]], with a hat-trick from Bale and a goal from Benzema ensuring the Madrid side the win.<ref>[http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1385442307230/noticia/Cronica/4-0:_A_rout_and_a_Bale_hat-trick.htm Real Madrid CF | Official Website] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203094953/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1385442307230/noticia/Cronica/4-0%3A_A_rout_and_a_Bale_hat-trick.htm |date=3 December 2013 }}</ref>

===December===
Real Madrid began December against [[CD Olímpic de Xàtiva|Olímpic de Xàtiva]] in the [[2013–14 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]] round of 32, with the game ending 0–0.<ref>[http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1386297098794/noticia/Cronica/0-0:_Draw_in_cup_opener.htm Real Madrid CF | Official Website] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131210220255/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1386297098794/noticia/Cronica/0-0%3A_Draw_in_cup_opener.htm |date=10 December 2013 }}</ref>

Madrid then faced Copenhagen away for their sixth Champions League group match, with the game ending 0–2 to Real. Goals from [[Luka Modrić]] and Ronaldo ensured Madrid the win. Ronaldo's goal set the new record for most goals scored in the Champions League group stages, with nine.<ref>[https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0210-0e87d7d9ecd4-e32ca293fbf2-1000--record-breaker-ronaldo-helps-madrid-end-on-high/ Record-breaker Ronaldo helps Madrid end on high – UEFA Champions League – News – UEFA.com<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> The match was Madrid's final of the group stage, and they were the only team in their group to progress to the knockout round undefeated.

''Los Blancos'' then faced [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]] away on the 14th. Madrid were down 2–0 in the first 40 minutes and were reduced to ten men (Sergio Ramos was dismissed at the stroke of half time), but were able to come away with a draw as Isco and Pepe scored to salvage a point.<ref>[http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1202817745826/1386888128005/noticia/Cronica/2-2:_A_draw_with_ten_men_in_Pamplona.htm Real Madrid CF | Official Website] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131215012727/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1202817745826/1386888128005/noticia/Cronica/2-2%3A_A_draw_with_ten_men_in_Pamplona.htm |date=15 December 2013 }}</ref>

In a midweek clash, Real faced Olímpic de Xàtiva in the second leg of the Copa del Rey, this time winning 2–0 at home and progressing further in the competition. A goal from Asier Illarramendi along with a penalty from Di María gave Madrid the goals, and the side was able to progress into the round of 16.<ref>[http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1387397997239/noticia/Cronica/2-0:_A_win_and_through_to_round_of_16.htm Real Madrid CF | Official Website] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131219042356/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1387397997239/noticia/Cronica/2-0%3A_A_win_and_through_to_round_of_16.htm |date=19 December 2013 }}</ref>

Madrid then faced Valencia away in La Liga, with Real winning 2–3. Goals from Ronaldo, Di María and Jesé gave the Madrid side the three points to climb up the La Liga table, along with going through the final two months of 2013 undefeated.<ref>[http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1387552390966/noticia/Cronica/2-3:_Win_in_the_Mestalla_to_end_the_year.htm Real Madrid CF | Official Website] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131224093834/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1387552390966/noticia/Cronica/2-3%3A_Win_in_the_Mestalla_to_end_the_year.htm |date=24 December 2013 }}</ref>

===January===
Madrid officially kicked off 2014 in a La Liga home match against [[Celta de Vigo]]. Madrid had failed to score in the first half, but a Benzema goal in the 67th minute broke the deadlock. Real, however, were not finished, as two goals from Ronaldo, one in the 82nd and another in stoppage time of the second half, gave the Madrid side another three points.<ref>[http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1388703010388/noticia/Cronica/3-0:_Big_win_to_start_the_year.htm Real Madrid CF | Official Website] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140107061115/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1388703010388/noticia/Cronica/3-0%3A_Big_win_to_start_the_year.htm |date=7 January 2014 }}</ref>

Real's second match was against Osasuna in the Copa del Rey round of 16, with the first leg being played at the Santiago Bernabéu. A 17th-minute goal from Benzema, along with a 60th-minute strike from youth star Jesé gave the Madrid side a 2–0 aggregate advantage heading into the second leg.<ref>[http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/First_Team/1193040487651/1389276963210/noticia/Cronica/2-0:_Real_Madrid_take_lead_into_the_second_leg.htm Real Madrid CF | Official Website] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140112153218/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/First_Team/1193040487651/1389276963210/noticia/Cronica/2-0%3A_Real_Madrid_take_lead_into_the_second_leg.htm |date=12 January 2014 }}</ref>

Madrid's third game of January came in La Liga, with Real visiting [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] away. A goal from centre-back Pepe was all that was required for Madrid to collect three points in a 0–1 win.<ref>[http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1389550269509/noticia/Cronica/0-1:_Hard_fought_win_with_a_goal_from_Pepe.htm Real Madrid CF | Official Website] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140112234150/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1389550269509/noticia/Cronica/0-1%3A_Hard_fought_win_with_a_goal_from_Pepe.htm |date=12 January 2014 }}</ref>

Madrid then had to focus themselves on their second leg Copa del Rey round of 16 clash away at Osasuna. Madrid again won this game 0–2, with goals from Ronaldo and Di María, who scored in the 21st and 56th minutes respectively.<ref>[http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1193040487651/1389820886968/noticia/Cronica/0-2:_Goals_from_Ronaldo_and_Di_Maria_seal_win.htm Real Madrid CF | Official Website] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140117011152/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1193040487651/1389820886968/noticia/Cronica/0-2%3A_Goals_from_Ronaldo_and_Di_Maria_seal_win.htm |date=17 January 2014 }}</ref> This win meant Real had progressed into the quarter-finals of the Copa del Rey.

Real Madrid then faced Real Betis away, with the match ending in a resounding 0–5 victory to ''Los Blancos''. Ronaldo scored a powerful long shot and assisted Morata with a bicycle kick, while the other goals were scored by Bale, Benzema, and Di María, helping collect another three points. This win propelled Madrid to joint top of La Liga.<ref>[http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1389882094689/noticia/Cronica/0-5:_Real_Madrid_win_big_to_go_joint_top.htm Real Madrid CF | Official Website] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140120211702/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1389882094689/noticia/Cronica/0-5%3A_Real_Madrid_win_big_to_go_joint_top.htm |date=20 January 2014 }}</ref>

Madrid faced Espanyol in the quarter-finals of the Copa del Rey, earning a 0–1 away result with a Benzema goal.<ref>[http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1390084246405/noticia/Cronica/0-1:_Benzema_gives_his_team_the_lead_in_the_tie.htm Real Madrid CF | Official Website] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140122084804/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1390084246405/noticia/Cronica/0-1%3A_Benzema_gives_his_team_the_lead_in_the_tie.htm |date=22 January 2014 }}</ref>

Real then faced 17th-placed Granada in a routine 2–0 home win. The goals came from Ronaldo and Benzema in the 56th and 74th minute respectively. The win propelled the Madrid side to the top of La Liga.<ref>[http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1390613772261/noticia/Cronica/2-0:_Deserved_win_and_top_of_La_Liga.htm Real Madrid CF | Official Website] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140128054559/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1390613772261/noticia/Cronica/2-0%3A_Deserved_win_and_top_of_La_Liga.htm |date=28 January 2014 }}</ref>

Madrid's final match of January came as a 1–0 home win against Espanyol in the quarter-finals of the Copa del Rey. Youth project Jesé scored early on, and Madrid were able to hang on tight until the end, winning 2–0 on aggregate and progressing to the semi-finals.<ref>[http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1390909190853/noticia/Cronica/1-0:Through_to_the_semi-finals_with_a_Jese_goal.htm Real Madrid CF | Official Website] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140131081519/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1390909190853/noticia/Cronica/1-0%3AThrough_to_the_semi-finals_with_a_Jese_goal.htm |date=31 January 2014 }}</ref>

===February===
Madrid kicked off February with a disappointing 1–1 draw against fourth-placed Athletic Bilbao, with Jesé scoring the lone goal for Real. They finished on an even sourer note, as Ronaldo was sent off in the 75th minute.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20140202225846/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1391122165588/noticia/Cronica/1-1:_Draw_in_San_Mames_with_a_Jese_goal.htm|title=Real Madrid CF {{!}} Official Website}}</ref>

Madrid were drawn to face fierce rivals Atlético Madrid in the semi-finals of the Copa del Rey. Real were without the suspended Ronaldo, but their star Portuguese forward was not required, as they won at home 3–0.<ref>[http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1391549277111/noticia/Cronica/3-0:_Real_Madrid_take_big_step_towards_final.htm Real Madrid CF | Official Website] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140209172748/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1391549277111/noticia/Cronica/3-0%3A_Real_Madrid_take_big_step_towards_final.htm |date=9 February 2014 }}</ref> Goals came from centre-back Pepe, winger Jesé and Argentinian forward Ángel Di María.

Real Madrid then faced Villarreal in La Liga, winning 4–2 at home. Goals from Bale, a brace from Benzema along with another strike from Jesé gave Madrid the win, but [[Mario Gaspar Pérez|Mario]] and [[Giovani dos Santos]] goals for Villarreal denied ''Los Blancos'' a clean sheet. This was Ronaldo's final match suspended, meaning he would be available in the second leg of the Copa del Rey clash against Atlético.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20140208225815/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1391768133266/noticia/Cronica/4-2:_Benzema_brace_seals_win.htm|title=Real Madrid CF {{!}} Official Website}}</ref>

Real's fourth match of February was their away leg clash against Atlético in the Copa del Rey. Returning star Ronaldo gave Real Madrid the win, with two converted penalties.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20140212025831/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1392178643028/noticia/Cronica/0-2:_Win_and_through_to_the_cup_final.htm|title=Real Madrid CF {{!}} Official Website}}</ref> These two goals meant Ronaldo had netted an impressive 34 goals in all competitions. Madrid's victory ensured they would face Barcelona in ''El Clásico'' for the [[2014 Copa del Rey Final|Copa del Rey final]] at the [[Mestalla Stadium]].

Real Madrid then faced Getafe in La Liga, away at the [[Coliseum Alfonso Pérez]]. Madrid comfortably cruised through the match, winning 0–3 with a goal from Jesé, who had scored in his last three La Liga matches, along with goals from Benzema and Modrić, and the win placed the Madrid side in second, on level points with Barcelona and Atlético Madrid.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20140216194521/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo_en/1392439114967/noticia/Cronica/0-3:_Real_Madrid_win_and_stay_joint_leaders.htm|title=Real Madrid CF {{!}} Official Website}}</ref>

The next match for Real Madrid proved to be vital, as winning would allow them to top La Liga, something the Spanish giants have not done for 15 months, but would only occur if Barcelona and Atlético Madrid lose. They faced Elche at home, winning 3–0 with a ''golazo'' from Gareth Bale, who struck from thirty yards out, along with goals from Illaramendi and Isco. Madrid's victory, along with Barcelona losing 3–1 to Real Sociedad and Atlético losing 3–0 to Osasuna, allowed them to top La Liga by three points.<ref>[http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/02/3-0-goleada-y-liderato-provisional 3–0: Win and to think Schalke | Real Madrid CF]</ref>

Madrid's last match of February was the first leg of their last 16 Champions League clash against [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]] away. The match turned out to be a seven-goal thriller for Madrid, as they won 1–6, effectively killing off the second leg and virtually guaranteeing Madrid a spot in the last eight of the competition. Braces were all scored by the returning Ronaldo, winger Bale and striker Benzema. However, a volley from [[Klaas-Jan Huntelaar]] in the 90th minute denied Madrid a clean sheet, along with ending captain and goalkeeper [[Iker Casillas]]' record of going over 900 minutes without conceding.<ref>[https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2011862--schalke-vs-real-madrid/ UEFA Champions League 2014 – Schalke-Real Madrid – UEFA.com<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

===March===
Real had a chance to extend their lead at the top of the table, should they win in ''El Derbi madrileño'' in La Liga against Atlético Madrid. Benzema scored early on to give Real the lead, before [[Koke (footballer, born 1992)|Koke]] equalised, slotting into the bottom left corner. Koke also assisted the second of Atlético's goal, which was scored by [[Gabi (footballer, born 1983)|Gabi]], who found the top left corner. Looking like a win for Real's bitter rivals, Cristiano Ronaldo scored and equalised and the game ended 2–2. Real gained a point and maintained the status quo at the top of La Liga, but now only carried a one-point lead over Barcelona.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/03/2-2-real-madrid-stay-top-with-a-draw-at-the-calderon |title=2–2: Real Madrid stay top with a draw at the Calderón &#124; Real Madrid CF |publisher=Real Madrid C.F. |date=3 May 2014 |access-date=24 June 2017}}</ref>

Real's second match of March was also their second La Liga match of March, as the leaders took on Levante. Ronaldo jumped highest to powerfully head in Di María's left-wing corner and Marcelo doubled their lead shortly after the restart. Levante were reduced to ten men after [[David Navarro (footballer)|David Navarro]] fought with an opponent. Real tripled their lead after [[Nikolaos Karabelas]] slid the ball in his own net. The win pushed Real three points clear at the top of La Liga, along with being four points above rivals Barcelona.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/03/3-0-levante-downed-and-back-on-top |title=3–0: Levante downed and back on top &#124; Real Madrid CF |publisher=Real Madrid C.F. |access-date=24 June 2017}}</ref>

Madrid had a chance to propel their lead over Barcelona, who had dominated the league in the previous seasons, should they beat Málaga. Barça suffered a shock defeat at the hands of Real Valladolid, and should Real win, the Madrid side would be seven points clear at the top over their fierce rivals. A strike from Ronaldo gave Madrid an early advantage, but many shots went amiss and the game finished in a close 0–1 victory to the Madrid side.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/03/0-1-the-league-leaders-make-no-mistake-in-la-rosaleda |title=0–1: The league leaders make no mistake in La Rosaleda &#124; Real Madrid CF |publisher=Real Madrid C.F. |date=15 March 2014 |access-date=24 June 2017}}</ref>

Madrid subsequently hosted Schalke 04 for the second leg of their Champions League last 16 clash, with Madrid already boasting a 6–1 aggregate lead. A strike from Ronaldo just after the 20th minute gave Real the lead only for [[Tim Hoogland]] to equalize, and the teams went into half time at 1–1. Madrid continued to pile on the pressure and were ultimately rewarded after Ronaldo found the net again in the 74th minute. Morata scored another to end the game at 3–1. Winning at a combined score of 9–2 on both legs, Madrid progressed to the next round of the tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2011868--real-madrid-vs-schalke/ |title=UEFA Champions League 2013/14 – History – Real Madrid-Schalke – |publisher=UEFA |access-date=24 June 2017}}</ref>

Madrid then hosted fierce rivals Barcelona, who were beginning to hit form and pile on the pressure to ''Los Blancos''. In what could be called as one of the most entertaining ''Clásicos'' of all time, a seven-goal thriller was played. [[Andrés Iniesta]] gave Barça the lead in the seventh minute, before two strikes from Karim Benzema in quick succession reversed the fortunes. [[Lionel Messi]] scored an equaliser, but Ronaldo gave Madrid the advantage netting home a penalty. Messi equalised again after a challenge from Madrid's defender Sergio Ramos resulted in a penalty and Ramos being sent off in the 63rd minute, along with converting another penalty, which completed the hat-trick for the Argentinian, along with him breaking the record for the number of goals scored in ''El Clásico''. The game was also notorious for dodgy officiating and missed chances, and it was named one of the most controversial matches ever.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/03/3-4-real-madrid-lose-in-a-controversy-packed-clasico |title=3–4: Real Madrid lose in a controversy-packed Clásico &#124; Real Madrid CF |publisher=Real Madrid C.F. |date=23 March 2014 |access-date=24 June 2017}}</ref>

Madrid then travelled to Sevilla, hoping to move up the La Liga table and keep pressure on their title rivals. Madrid found the net early, thanks to Ronaldo, before [[Carlos Bacca]] netted in just under 20 minutes. Bacca scored again in the 72nd minute, giving Sevilla the win and putting a dent in Madrid's title challenge.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/03/2-1-the-sanchez-pizjuan-watches-real-madrid-stumble-in-the-fight-for-the-liga |title=2–1: The Sánchez Pizjuán watches Real Madrid stumble in the fight for the Liga &#124; Real Madrid CF |publisher=Real Madrid C.F. |date=26 March 2014 |access-date=24 June 2017}}</ref>

Madrid's final match of March was at home to Rayo Vallecano, a game which Madrid dominated, scoring five in the process. Ronaldo netted early, before right-back Dani Carvajal scored in the second half, after which Bale added a brace, along with a strike from Morata, giving Madrid the three points and reclaiming back the winning momentum after suffering back-to-back defeats.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/03/5-0-real-madrid-remain-in-the-hunt-for-title-after-goalfest- |title=5–0: Real Madrid remain in the hunt for title after goalfest &#124; Real Madrid CF |publisher=Real Madrid C.F. |date=29 March 2014 |access-date=24 June 2017}}</ref>

===April===
Real Madrid began April by hosting [[Borussia Dortmund]] in the first leg of the Champions League quarter-finals at the Santiago Bernabéu, three days after the thrashing of Vallecano. Having decimated Schalke 04 in the round of 16, Madrid hosted last year's Champions League [[2013 UEFA Champions League Final|finalists]]. Furthermore, Dortmund had defeated Real [[2012–13 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Semi-finals|4–3 on aggregate]] in last season's semi-finals, and ''Los Blancos'' were eager to get their revenge. Bale opened the scoring in the third minute, before Isco added another, with Madrid leading 2–0 at half time. Ronaldo added another before Madrid played calm to win comprehensively. The 3–0 Madrid victory required Dortmund to score four goals in the next round to progress further in the competition.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2011872--real-madrid-vs-b-dortmund/ |title=UEFA Champions League 2013/14 – History – Real Madrid-Dortmund – |publisher=UEFA |access-date=24 June 2017}}</ref>

Madrid's second match of April was against Real Sociedad. Goals from Illarramendi, Bale, Pepe and Morata helped Real to a calm 4–0 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/04/0-4-real-madrid-let-loose-in-anoeta-and-stay-in-the-fight-for-the-liga |title=0–4: Real Madrid let loose in Anoeta and stay in the fight for the Liga &#124; Real Madrid CF |publisher=Real Madrid C.F. |date=5 April 2014 |access-date=24 June 2017}}</ref>

Madrid travelled away to Dortmund for the second leg of the Champions League quarter-finals, and lost 2–0 after an impressive solo performance from [[Marco Reus]]. His efforts fell to fruition, however, as Madrid progressed into the semi-finals of the competition, where they would face last year's winners in [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2011878--b-dortmund-vs-real-madrid/ |title=UEFA Champions League 2013/14 – History – Dortmund-Real Madrid – |publisher=UEFA |date=8 April 2014 |access-date=24 June 2017}}</ref>

Madrid's fourth match of April was against Almería, and the match was the second in a row where Madrid scored four goals, as another 4–0 win kept them in the race for the title, thanks to goals from Di María, Bale, Isco and Morata.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/04/4-0-goal-fest-four-days-before-the-cup-final |title=4–0: Goal-fest four days before the cup final &#124; Real Madrid CF |publisher=Real Madrid C.F. |access-date=24 June 2017}}</ref>

Madrid's fifth match of April was against fierce rivals Barcelona in the [[2014 Copa del Rey Final|final]] of the Copa del Rey. Superstar Ronaldo was injured and unavailable for the game, but Madrid boasted a proud record, as they were the only side in the competition not to concede, and found the net early thanks to Di María. Heading into the late stages of the match, [[Marc Bartra]] scored for Barça, levelling the scores. As it looked like the match would be contested in extra time, a brilliant solo goal from Bale late on ensured Madrid the trophy, lifting their 19th Copa del Rey title.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/04/1-2-real-madrid-reign-supreme-once-again-in-mestalla |title=1–2: Real Madrid reign supreme once again in Mestalla &#124; Real Madrid CF |publisher=Real Madrid C.F. |date=16 April 2014 |access-date=24 June 2017}}</ref>

The next fixture was a crucial one for ''Los Blancos'' as they faced the [[2012–13 UEFA Champions League|defending champions]] of the European Cup and perennial rivals Bayern Munich in the Champions League semi-finals. Real won thanks to a Benzema goal in a tightly contested game.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/27119749|title = Real Madrid 1-0 Bayern Munich|work = BBC Sport}}</ref>

In between two crucial battles against Bayern, Madrid easily dispatched of Osasuna 4–0 in the league thanks to a brace from Ronaldo, which consisted of two marvelous long shots, plus goals by Ramos and Carvajal. This was Real's third consecutive league victory with at least four goals scored and none conceded.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/27161593|title = Real Madrid 4-0 Osasuna|work = BBC Sport}}</ref>

''Los Blancos'' capped their successful month by progressing to the [[2014 UEFA Champions League Final|Champions League final]] for the first time in [[2002 UEFA Champions League Final|12 years]] after defeating the defending champions. The Whites dominated the game, winning the semi-final matchup 5–0 on aggregate. Victory over Bayern meant that Madrid had defeated both finalists of the previous Champions League season en route to the final.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/27193338|title = Bayern Munich 0-4 Real Madrid (Agg 0-5)|work = BBC Sport}}</ref>

===May===
In terms of league performance, May was somewhat a disappointment for Real as the team won only one out of four games and failed to clinch the title, finishing three points behind rivals Atlético Madrid and level on points with Barcelona but below on head-to-head tiebreaking criteria. As a result, ''Los Blancos'' finished the season third, but in title contention throughout the season. Besides, Madrid scored the most goals (104) out of all teams in their league campaign and was second only to Barça on goal differential (+66 to +67).

The league fixtures of the month were a 2–2 home tie with Valencia (with a 90+2 backheel equalizer from Ronaldo), a 1–1 away tie with Valladolid (with the home team equalizing late in the match), a 0–2 away defeat to Celta (that ruined Real's hopes for the title), and a 3–1 win over Espanyol on the last matchday.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/27276497|title = Real Madrid 2-2 Valencia CF|work = BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/27301055|title = Real Valladolid 1-1 Real Madrid|work = BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/27301107|title = Celta Vigo 2-0 Real Madrid|work = BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/27422375|title = Real Madrid 3-1 Espanyol|work = BBC Sport}}</ref>

Winning a long-awaited ''La Décima'' would be much more than a perfect consolation for ''Los Blancos'' and they ultimately brought a record-extending tenth European Cup title from [[Lisbon]], although their path was anything but easy. [[Diego Godín]] opened the scoring for Atlético in the first half and the Madrid team was on the run to accomplishing their first [[Double (association football)#European Double|continental double]] in history up to the injury time of the second half when [[Sergio Ramos]] scored an all-important head ball equalizer after a corner kick. In the extra time, it was Real, Real, and only Real as ''Los Blancos'' obliterated the distraught rivals by scoring three unanswered goals in its second half (courtesy of [[Gareth Bale|Bale]], [[Marcelo (footballer, born 1988)|Marcelo]], and [[Cristiano Ronaldo|Ronaldo]]) and triumphed in the competition.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/27383593|title = Real Madrid 4-1 Atletico Madrid|work = BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/05/24/sixth-anniversary-of-la-decima|title = Sixth anniversary of la Décima &#124; Real Madrid CF}}</ref> Overall, Ronaldo scored 51 goals (31 in La Liga, a record 17 in the Champions League, and three in the Copa del Rey) to become the team's top scorer for the fifth consecutive season. The Portuguese would go even further in the [[2014–15 Real Madrid CF season|next season]], scoring 61 goals in all competitions and breaking his own record from [[2011–12 Real Madrid CF season|2011–12]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2465540-comparing-cristiano-ronaldos-201415-stats-to-his-201314-numbers|title = Comparing Cristiano Ronaldo's 2014/15 Stats to His 2013/14 Numbers|website = [[Bleacher Report]]}}</ref>
